t: Section 901 (a)(1) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking out “or of Mexican border service” and inserting in lieu thereof of Mexican border service, or of service after January 31, 1955”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment to title 38 that extends a veterans' provision to cover service after January 31, 1955. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation reading here beyond the fact that it affects veterans' eligibility, which is a benefits matter and not participation in a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “or of Mexican border service” and inserting in lieu thereof of Mexican border service, or of service after January 31, 1955”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to the definition of qualifying military service for veterans' benefits. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. It simply changes the eligibility criteria for a benefit program.
qwen_block.s: Section 901 (a)(1) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking out “or of Mexican border service” and inserting in lieu thereof of Mexican border service, or of service after January 31, 1955”.

opus.w: This amendment only adds service after January 31, 1955 to the qualifying service periods in 38 U.S.C. 901(a)(1). It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. Changing who is eligible for a benefit is not participation, so nothing in the section is even on-topic.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The only possible trap is reading any amendment to a benefit provision as a federal decision process. That reading fails here. The section just adds a new period of service ("service after January 31, 1955") to an existing eligibility rule in title 38. It doesn't mention consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body, or any right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment to the eligibility criteria for veterans' benefits. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or receive input from any outside party (such as states, tribes, the public, or experts) before making a decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, and this text merely changes the statutory definition of qualifying service without establishing any participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 901 (a)(1) of title 38, United States Code, is amended by striking out “or of Mexican border service” and inserting in lieu thereof of Mexican border service, or of service after January 31, 1955”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that changing eligibility criteria for veterans' benefits involves public participation because it affects individuals. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and does not include legislative amendments to benefit eligibility as "participation" in the sense of consultation or coordination with outside parties before a decision. This section is purely a legislative amendment to a statute, not a procedural requirement for the government to consult with outsiders.
